title: M&A Theory Learning Map
description: A concise theory path for VFCC preparation across historical analysis, valuation, and board-level recommendation.

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.title: Historical Analysis and Forecast Architecture
weeks.summary: Build a traceable three-year historical model and a driver-based five-year forecast that can support valuation, due diligence, and a board-level recommendation.

topics.title: Source-Controlled History
topics.summary: Create a consistent historical dataset in fixed units and periods, with every reported fact traceable to a filing, note, or case exhibit.
learningQuestions: Can five sampled historical figures be traced to their exact source?
Do the model totals reconcile to the published statements?
subtopics: Three-year income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow history
Units, fiscal periods, and actual-versus-forecast labels

topics.title: Operating Economics
topics.summary: Translate reported statements into operating drivers and explain how price, volume, mix, capacity, costs, and cash conversion shape performance.
learningQuestions: Which operating drivers explain the historical revenue and margin bridges?
What evidence separates a durable trend from a temporary movement?
subtopics: Revenue bridge: price, volume, mix, acquisitions, foreign exchange, and disposals
Margin bridge: pricing, input costs, utilisation, labour, and overhead absorption
Investment bridge: maintenance and growth capital expenditure

topics.title: Working Capital
topics.summary: Model operating working capital as a cash cycle, keeping cash and financing items separate from day-to-day operating balances.
learningQuestions: Why can improving receivable days still coexist with weak revenue quality?
Which operating flow is the correct denominator for each days calculation?
subtopics: Seasonality, ageing, factoring, and supplier finance

topics.title: Normalisation and Quality
topics.summary: Keep reported and adjusted performance separate, and test whether earnings, assets, liabilities, and cash conversion represent sustainable economics.
learningQuestions: Is each adjustment supported by recurrence, operating relevance, cash effect, and forecast treatment?
How should weak information quality change assumptions, valuation range, or the price ceiling?
subtopics: Accruals, provisions, estimates, and disclosure consistency

topics.title: Driver-Based Forecast
topics.summary: Build the forecast in causal order so that operational assumptions flow through revenue, costs, working capital, investment, tax, and financing.
learningQuestions: What operational evidence supports each forecast driver?
Do changes to a key assumption flow through the complete model?
subtopics: Variable, semi-variable, and fixed operating costs
Capital expenditure, depreciation, and asset roll-forwards
Accounting tax, cash tax, financing, and balance items

topics.title: Scenarios and Controls
topics.summary: Use coherent base, upside, and downside narratives, with traceable assumptions, controlled circularity, and a prominent error-check panel.
learningQuestions: Does each scenario tell a plausible operating story rather than apply a uniform haircut?
Can an independent reviewer detect stale links, hard-coded outputs, and unintended circularity?
subtopics: Base, upside, and downside operating narratives

topics.title: EV-to-Equity Bridge
topics.summary: Translate enterprise value to equity value using a documented and internally consistent classification of cash, debt, leases, investments, and other claims.
learningQuestions: Is each bridge item treated consistently with the forecast and valuation method?
Which bridge classification is most judgmental and what evidence would resolve it?
subtopics: Pensions, minority interests, and non-operating investments
Supplier finance, provisions, and tax liabilities

weeks.label: Week 3
weeks.title: Valuation and Transaction Pricing
weeks.summary: Convert operating forecasts into a defensible valuation range, reconcile multiple methods, and define a price boundary that reflects risk and deal logic.

topics.title: Valuation Frame
topics.summary: Define the asset being valued, the valuation date, the ownership claim, and the information available before choosing a method.
learningQuestions: Are enterprise and equity value kept distinct throughout the analysis?
Which valuation methods fit the business and the decision?

topics.title: Discounted Cash Flow
topics.summary: Value the operating business from forecast free cash flow, using internally consistent cash flows, discount rates, and timing conventions.
learningQuestions: Do the cash-flow definition and discount rate measure the same claim?
Which forecast assumptions drive most of the present value?

topics.title: Discount Rate
topics.summary: Estimate a discount rate that matches the currency, risk, leverage, and cash-flow claim without hiding operating uncertainty inside one premium.
learningQuestions: Are risk-free rate, beta, risk premium, and cost of debt measured consistently?
How does target capital structure affect WACC?
subtopics: Cost of debt and tax shield
Currency, country risk, and capital structure

topics.title: Terminal Value
topics.summary: Model a mature steady state that respects reinvestment, growth, returns on capital, and the economic life of the business.
learningQuestions: Is perpetual growth supportable in the chosen currency and market?
Does terminal reinvestment support the assumed growth?

topics.title: Trading Comparables
topics.summary: Select genuinely comparable public companies, normalise the metrics, and interpret observed multiples in light of growth, risk, and profitability.
learningQuestions: What makes a peer economically comparable rather than merely similar by label?
Are numerator and denominator definitions consistent?
subtopics: Outliers, accounting differences, and implied values

topics.title: Precedent Transactions
topics.summary: Use prior deals carefully by separating market conditions, control, expected synergies, and transaction-specific terms from stand-alone value.
learningQuestions: Are the selected transactions comparable in timing, size, geography, and economics?
What portion of an observed premium may reflect expected synergies or competition?

topics.title: Synergies and Price
topics.summary: Separate stand-alone value from buyer-specific synergies and translate valuation evidence into a range, walk-away price, and negotiation logic.
learningQuestions: Who can realise each synergy and what will it cost?
How much expected value can be paid away before the buyer destroys value?
subtopics: Revenue, cost, tax, and financing synergies

weeks.label: Week 6
weeks.title: Recommendation and Board Defence
weeks.summary: Integrate strategy, valuation, financing, risk, and execution into a clear recommendation that can withstand board-level questions.

topics.title: Decision Thesis
topics.summary: State the decision, the strategic and financial reasons for it, and the conditions that would change the recommendation.
learningQuestions: Can the recommendation be understood before the supporting detail?
Does each reason link to evidence and a decision consequence?

topics.title: Deal Structure
topics.summary: Design price form, financing, protections, and governance so that transaction terms respond to identified value drivers and risks.
learningQuestions: Which risks belong in price, structure, diligence, or a contractual protection?
How do financing and consideration affect risk, control, and value transfer?
subtopics: Cash, shares, debt, and mixed consideration
Financing capacity and pro forma leverage

topics.title: Risk Case
topics.summary: Prioritise the uncertainties that could change value or feasibility and connect each risk to evidence, exposure, mitigation, and ownership.
learningQuestions: Which risks could invalidate the base case or prevent closing?
Is each mitigation specific enough to monitor after approval?
subtopics: Commercial, financial, operational, legal, and execution risk

topics.title: Integration and Value
topics.summary: Translate the deal thesis into an executable value-capture plan with accountable owners, realistic timing, investment needs, and safeguards for the base business.
learningQuestions: Which actions must occur for the valuation case to be realised?
How will the team distinguish realised value from market or base-business effects?
subtopics: Synergy initiatives, costs, timing, and owners
Customer, talent, systems, and culture risks

topics.title: Advisory Memo
topics.summary: Write a concise board-level memo that leads with the recommendation and uses exhibits to make the evidence, valuation, risks, and conditions easy to audit.
learningQuestions: Can a decision-maker follow the logic without opening the model?
Do exhibits answer a decision question rather than merely display analysis?

topics.title: Presentation Story
topics.summary: Turn the analysis into a focused sequence of decision messages, with readable exhibits and disciplined allocation of presentation time.
learningQuestions: Does every slide advance the board's decision?
Can the team explain the recommendation, valuation, and principal risk within the time limit?
subtopics: Readable charts, tables, and model outputs

topics.title: Q&A Defence
topics.summary: Defend the recommendation by answering the question first, supporting it with model evidence, and stating uncertainty without losing the decision boundary.
learningQuestions: Can every team member explain the model's critical assumptions and checks?
What evidence would cause the team to change its view?
subtopics: Challenges to strategy, valuation, and execution
Cold review, rehearsal, and response ownership
